logo_override.validation_detail: webfetch returned 'Image fetched successfully', confirming HTTP 200 plus a real image content type. Declared by the page itself as <link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/content/dam/uoc-restricted/icons/apple-icon-180x180.png">. Decoded and rendered: the University of Canterbury lockup - the serif 'UC' monogram beside the University's red coat of arms - in UC brand red #CC0011 on an opaque white field. The artwork is a saturated mid-dark red on white with no alpha channel, so it is legible on a light card and there is no white-on-transparent variant.

notes: Important trap here, and the reason a naive scan of the UC header fails. The header brand is an SVG sprite: . I fetched that sprite and it does contain the real artwork - every path is fill="#CC0011" (UC red) over an opaque plate - so it is NOT a white-on-transparent wordmark. But the file contains only elements (id sm-logo / lg-logo / xl-logo) and no directly renderable content, so loading it as an yields a blank image even though it returns HTTP 200 with an image content type. Reporting it would have been a technically-probed but visually-empty logo, so I rejected it and used the raster lockup instead, which renders standalone. Rule 1 note: the asset lives under /content/dam/uoc-restricted/... - 'restricted' is an AEM DAM permissions segment, but the host is still www.canterbury.ac.nz, the awarding university itself, so it is same_registrable_domain and not a third-party CDN. Rule 2 satisfied: the UC Doctoral Scholarship is centrally funded by the University, so the University's own mark is correct. This is a crest-plus-wordmark lockup rather than a bare favicon glyph, which is what the brief prefers. DATA ISSUE for the merge, not for me to fix: the shard record's official_source field contains mojibake - it reads 'Te Whare WÄnanga o Waitaha', which is UTF-8 bytes decoded as Latin-1; the correct string is 'Te Whare Wananga o Waitaha' ( macron on the first a). I did not edit the shard, per the instruction not to touch other repo files.
